text:
Predicates:
PerformsInTalentShow(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
AttendsSchoolEvents(x) ::: x attends and is very engaged with school events.
CommunityMember(x) ::: x is a member of the community.
InactiveMember(x) ::: x is an inactive and disinterested member of the community.
ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
WishesToFurtherCareer(x) ::: x wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities.
YoungChildOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
Bonnie ::: Bonnie.
Premises:
∀x (PerformsInTalentShow(x) → AttendsSchoolEvents(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (PerformsInTalentShow(x) ∨ (InactiveMember(x) ∧ CommunityMember(x))) ::: People either perform in school talent shows often or are inactive and disinterested members of their community.
∀x (ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x) → ¬Student(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (InactiveMember(x) ∧ CommunityMember(x) → ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members of the community chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeen(x) ∧ WishesToFurtherCareer(x) → Student(x)) ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers and educational opportunities are students who attend the school.
Bonnie ::: Bonni.
Conclusion:
(ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∨ (¬ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∧ PerformsInTalentShow(Bonnie))) → (WishesToFurtherCareer(Bonnie) ∧ YoungChildOrTeen(Bonnie) ∧ InactiveMember(Bonnie)) ::: If Bonnie either chaperones high school dances or, if she does not, she performs in school talent shows often, then Bonnie is both a young child or teenager who wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities and an inactive and disinterested member of the community.
